chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Jabalah, from Sayf, from Maymun al-Sayqal, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man was affected by janabah during the night, so he performed ghusl. Then when morning came, he looked and found janabah on his garment. He said: “All praise belongs to Allah, who has not left anything without a limit for it. If, when he rose for salat, he looked and saw nothing, then there is no repetition upon him. But if, when he rose, he did not look, then repetition is upon him.”
ai.seo_question: If someone performs ghusl for janabah and later finds impurity on his clothes, must he repeat the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who performed ghusl from janabah and later found traces of impurity on his garment after praying. If he had checked at the time of salat and saw nothing, he does not repeat the prayer; but if he failed to check, he must repeat it.
